category.description: the single best-fit matter type, judged by meaning not keywords. NDA: confidentiality agreements. Vendor: buying goods/services from a supplier on our paper. Contract Review: any other agreement to draft or review (MSA, SoW, amendment, renewal, counterparty paper). Privacy: DPAs, data incidents, privacy questions. Litigation: disputes, claims, notices of breach, court papers. Trademark: marks and brand. Policy/FAQ: a question about a policy or how to do something. General: anything else

sub_type.description: the specific flavour, e.g. 'custom NDA (no template)', 'standard mutual NDA', 'MSA', 'DPA'

complexity.description: judge from the ACTUAL request — deal value, bespoke terms, multi-party, cross-border all raise it; do not default by matter type

urgency.description: how time-critical the requester makes it sound

business_unit.description: the requesting business unit / department if stated or inferable

estimated_value.description: the deal/contract value as stated (in its own currency, do not convert), else null

key_asks.description: what the requester actually wants, in plain terms (e.g. 'draft a custom NDA, do not use the standard template')

missing_info.description: CRITICAL facts this matter type needs to be drafted or handled properly that the request does NOT provide — e.g. 'counterparty legal name', 'what the agreement is for'. Only facts WITHOUT which no one could start the work; anything negotiable or with a standard default (term, governing law, value) is NOT missing. Usually empty.

recommended_workflow_id.description: id of the single best-fit workflow from the catalog, or null if none fits or a human should route it

workflow_reasoning.description: one or two sentences on the workflow pick

confidence.description: 0..1 — honest confidence in this whole read

reasoning.description: one or two sentences summarising your understanding of the request

needs_human.description: true if ambiguous or high-stakes enough that a human should confirm the routing
